use: a horror beat whose subject stays hidden
request: A 20 second beat for my campfire-stories channel: something is under the dock, and we never see it.
intent: Horror fans should feel dread from what is not shown; the thing under the water must never appear.
goal: The viewer feels that something is holding the rope from below and never sees what it is.
promise: A quiet lake, and a rope that should not move.
arc: Still water and a girl at the dock's end, the rope snapping tight, rings on the water and a long silence, nothing surfacing.

events.text: The lake was flat as glass. Mara sat at the end of the dock, feet over the water.
events.knows: Mara at the end of the dock on a still lake.
events.look: Mara at the end of the dock, the water still

events.text: Then the rope tied to the post went tight.
events.knows: The rope from the post snapped taut.
events.look: the rope from the post snapping taut down into the water

events.text: Something below had taken hold of it.
events.knows: Something under the water holds the rope.
events.look: the dark water where the rope goes in; nothing but rings

holds.does: the rope trembles and rings spread from where it enters the water; nothing surfaces

events.text: She didn't move. Neither did whatever was holding on.
events.knows: Mara is frozen; the thing below holds still too.
events.look: Mara frozen, the rope taut and still

holds.does: nothing moves; the last ring fades

measure.derived: Derived once from the request, intent and audience; thresholds not named here take the defaults in bench/lib/settings.ts. Read sizes scale with how wide the frame looks: a classroom or meeting screen from the back looks narrower than a phone at arm's length, a laptop at a desk wider. A hold listed as still is one the plan asks to wait without motion. The thing under the water is meant to stay hidden, so the eye is not scored on it in e3, and the final hold is meant to be still.

context.attention: watching on purpose, in the dark
context.why: a story channel watched at night
